ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Three circular hoops are joined together so that they intersect at rightangles as shown. A ladybird lands on an intersection and crawls around the outside of the hoops by repeating this procedure: she travels along a quarter-circle, turns $90^{\circ}$ to the right, travels along a quarter-circle and turns $90^{\circ}$ to the left. Proceeding in this way, how many quarter-circles will she travel along before she first returns to her starting point? <image1>

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a spherical frame composed of three circular wide band-shaped hoops; they are like three mutually perpendicular great circles, intersecting one another at right angles at the intersection points. Such three great circles have a total of six pairwise intersection points, which can be regarded as three pairs of opposite points on the sphere. Each circular hoop is divided by these intersection points into four quarter-circle segments. Reasoning: According to the specified method, label the six intersection points as +x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z. The three circular hoops can be regarded as mutually perpendicular great circles respectively passing through these points; for example, one circular hoop passes through +x, +y, -x, -y, another passes through +y, +z, -y, -z, and another passes through +z, +x, -z, -x. Because the figure is symmetric, the starting point and initial direction may be chosen arbitrarily. Suppose the ladybug starts from +x and first goes along a quarter-circle to +y. Then according to the rule it alternately turns: first turn right, then turn left, and repeat. Along the outside, the route obtained in order is: +x → +y → -z → -x → -y → +z → +x. The six intermediate intersection points are not repeated, until after the sixth quarter-circle segment it returns to the starting point +x for the first time. Therefore before she first returns to the starting point, she has walked 6 quarter-circle segments.

method.method_draft: Model the picture as three mutually perpendicular great-circle hoops on a sphere. First label the six intersection points as opposite pairs, e.g. +x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z, where each hoop contains four of these points and is divided into quarter-circle arcs between adjacent labeled intersections. Choose any starting intersection and initial outside direction, for example start at +x and move one quarter-circle toward +y. At each intersection, apply the text rule alternately: after the first quarter turn 90° right onto the other hoop, after the next quarter turn 90° left, then repeat. Trace the resulting labeled route around the outside: +x → +y → -z → -x → -y → +z → +x. Count the quarter-circle arcs in this first closed route; there are 6.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是三个圆形宽带状的 hoop 组成的球形框架，它们像三条互相垂直的大圆，彼此在交点处成直角相交。这样的三个大圆共有六个两两相交的交点，可以看成球面上三对相对点。每个圆环都被这些交点分成四段 quarter-circle。

推理：按指定方法，把六个交点标为 +x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z。三个圆环可看作分别经过这些点的互相垂直的大圆，例如一个圆环经过 +x, +y, -x, -y，另一个经过 +y, +z, -y, -z，另一个经过 +z, +x, -z, -x。由于图形对称，可任选起点和初始方向。设瓢虫从 +x 出发，先沿一个 quarter-circle 到 +y。然后按规则交替转向：先右转，再左转，并重复。沿外侧依次得到路线：+x → +y → -z → -x → -y → +z → +x。中间六个交点都不重复，直到第六段 quarter-circle 后第一次回到起点 +x。因此她第一次回到起点前走过 6 段 quarter-circle。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is a direct labeled-graph tracing method using the geometry of three perpendicular hoops as an octahedral network. It is the natural single-solution route; variants would mostly be weak paraphrases unless they use a different formalism.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read from the image that the object consists of three circular hoops arranged like mutually perpendicular great circles, with intersections occurring at right angles and with quarter-circle arcs between successive intersections on each hoop.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text to know the ladybird starts at an intersection, travels one quarter-circle at a time, and alternates a 90° right turn then a 90° left turn after successive quarter-circles.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the bridge that three mutually perpendicular great circles have six intersection points and form the edge graph of an octahedron; a right or left turn at an intersection means switching from the current hoop to the other hoop through that intersection.
